verses.text: When Ahaziah's mother Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she set out to kill all the royal heirs.

But Jehosheba, King Joram's daughter and Ahaziah's sister, took Ahaziah's son Joash away from among the royal sons who were being killed. She put him and his nurse in a bedroom and hid him from Athaliah, so he wasn't killed.
Joash stayed hidden with her in the LORD's house for six years while Athaliah ruled the land.
In the seventh year, Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and the guard. He brought them to the LORD's house, made a covenant with them there, and showed them the king's son.
Then he gave them these orders: “Here's what you must do. A third of those of you coming on duty on the Sabbath will guard the palace.
A third will stand at the Sur Gate, and a third at the gate behind the guard. Together you'll keep watch over the palace and block access.
The two companies going off duty on the Sabbath will stand guard around the king at the LORD's house.
Surround the king, each man with his weapon in hand. Anyone who breaks through your ranks must be killed. Stay with the king wherever he goes.”
The commanders of hundreds did exactly as Jehoiada the priest ordered. Each brought his men to the priest, both those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty.
The priest gave the commanders the spears and shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the LORD's house.
The guards stood with weapons in hand, from one side of the temple to the other, by the altar and the building, with the king inside their ranks.
Jehoiada brought out the king's son, put the crown on him, and gave him the covenant. They made him king and anointed him. Then they clapped and shouted, “Long live the king!”
When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people, she went to the crowd in the LORD's house.

She saw the king standing by the pillar, as was customary, with the commanders and trumpeters beside him. The people of the land were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, “Treason! Treason!”

Jehoiada the priest told the commanders in charge of the army, “Take her out between the ranks and kill anyone who follows her with the sword.” The priest had said, “Don't let her be killed in the LORD's house.”
They seized her and took her out by the horses' entrance to the royal palace. She was killed there.
Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people, that they would be the LORD's people. He also made a covenant between the king and the people.

All the people of the land went to Baal's temple and tore it down. They smashed his altars and images to pieces and killed Mattan, Baal's priest, in front of the altars. Jehoiada appointed officers over the LORD's house.

Jehoiada took the commanders, the Carites, the guard, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the LORD's house. They entered the palace through the Guard Gate, and he sat on the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. Athaliah had been killed with the sword at the palace.
Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.
